Map a schema to data

Source: R/data-mapping.R
data-mapping.Rd

A schema's four core fields describe an analysis without reference to any dataset. It can also carry a reference to the data it runs on, and be mapped: every step given the variables it reads (inputs) and creates (outputs). Mapping is optional – gen_code() works on a schema without it. A mapped schema can be checked against its data before any code is generated, constrains the variable names the generated code uses, and lets draw_tines() draw data-flow edges.

A schema is in one of three states, and the state belongs to the whole schema, never to one step:

  • plain – no step has inputs/outputs;

  • incomplete – some steps do. What has been written is kept (and written to file), but nothing relies on it: it is not checked, not drawn and not given to gen_code(). A message names the steps still missing;

  • mapped – every step has both.

The functions:

  • update_data() sets the data reference: a data file, a "package::dataset" string, an R script that builds the data, or a data frame.

  • gen_io() drafts the inputs/outputs of every step with an LLM, for you to review. It is never called implicitly. This is the recommended way to map a schema: inputs and outputs written by hand are easy to get wrong, so a hand-written schema is best left unmapped.

  • update_io() sets the inputs/outputs of one step, to correct a drafted mapping. add_step() takes the same inputs/outputs arguments, and they can be written in the YAML file.

Every one of these re-checks the schema with validate_schema() and warns about any problem the change introduced, so a broken mapping is caught when it is made. See the "Mapping a schema to data" section of vignette("schema") for an overview.

Usage

update_data(schema, data, object = NULL)

update_io(schema, id, inputs = NULL, outputs = NULL)

gen_io(schema, data = NULL, object = NULL, model = "anthropic/claude-opus-4-5")

Arguments

schema

A schema object.

data

The data the schema runs on: a path to a data file (.csv, .rds, .rda), a "package::dataset" string, a path to an R script that creates the data, or a data frame. Only the column names and types are kept; the data itself is never stored on the schema. A data frame gives no reference that can be written to a file, so it is used for checking only.

object

For an R script, the name of the object the script creates that holds the data. If NULL, the script must create exactly one data frame.

id

The id of the step to update.

inputs, outputs

Character vectors of variable names; character(0) records that the step has none. NULL leaves the field unchanged, and NA clears it.

model

The LLM to use for gen_io(), as a string in "provider/model" form (e.g. "anthropic/claude-opus-4-5", "openai/gpt-5", "google_gemini/gemini-2.5-flash"), passed to ellmer::chat(). Defaults to "anthropic/claude-opus-4-5".

Value

A schema object.

See also

validate_schema() for what the checks cover.

Examples

hdi_data <- data.frame(
  life_exp = c(72, 81, 66),
  exp_sch = c(13, 16, 10),
  gni = c(9000, 42000, 3200)
)

# map each step by hand as you add it
schema <- build_schema("HDI", data = hdi_data) |>
  add_step(
    id = "step-scaling", decision = "apply min-max scaling",
    inputs = c("life_exp", "exp_sch", "gni"), outputs = "scaled"
  ) |>
  add_step(
    id = "step-combine", decision = "use the geometric mean",
    inputs = "scaled", outputs = "hdi"
  )

# map a plain schema by hand, one step at a time
plain <- example_hdi() |>
  update_io("step-scaling", inputs = c("life_exp", "exp_sch"), outputs = "scaled")
#> ℹ The mapping is incomplete: steps `step-education`, `step-combine` have no
#>   inputs/outputs yet (1 of 3 steps mapped). Until every step has them, they are
#>   kept but not checked or used.

# edit one step: renaming an output flags the step that still reads it
schema <- update_io(schema, "step-scaling", outputs = "df_scaled")
#> Warning: The schema's inputs/outputs have 1 problem:
#> ! Step `step-combine` reads `scaled`, which is neither a data column nor
#>   created by an earlier step.

# ...and fixed
schema <- update_io(schema, "step-combine", inputs = "df_scaled")

# point the schema at a dataset whose columns no longer match
renamed <- data.frame(life_exp = 70, exp_sch = 12, income = 8000)
schema <- update_data(schema, renamed)
#> Warning: The schema's inputs/outputs have 1 problem:
#> ! Step `step-scaling` reads `gni`, which is neither a data column nor created
#>   by an earlier step.

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Requires an LLM API key (e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY); not run automatically.
example_hdi() |>
  gen_io(data = hdi_data)
} # }
